description: Jonathan Dooley at New Mexico Institute of Mining and Technology publishes a minimal working example for correcting vector winds measured by a UAV-mounted Trisonica anemometer. The August 2024 Zenodo archive and linked GitHub repository provide Python code free under GPL 3.0. Inputs include measured wind components, vehicle velocity, pressure, temperature and heading. Outputs contain one-second averaged winds, horizontal errors, density, transect normals and cross-wind components. These quantities can prepare airborne methane measurements for industrial-emission and waste-facility dispersion simulations. Coverage depends on the user’s flight observations, not a fixed geographic grid. No related catalogue record explicitly covers this routine. Vehicle velocity must use East-North-Up coordinates, which may differ from the aircraft default; heading selection also changes processing. The README documents development with Python 3.11 but does not establish every package version. Sensor uncertainty and transformed-wind accuracy were not independently tested, and no code was executed.
